html:
The Himyarite Kingdom, or Himyar, was a kingdom in the highlands of southwest Arabia, in today's Yemen, from 110 BCE to 525 CE. Its capital was Zafar. On the map it appears from 1 CE to 500.

Himyar rose as the old incense kingdoms declined and trade moved to the Red Sea. Around 275 CE it conquered Saba, and soon after Hadramaut, uniting all of Yemen for the first time. Its kings then pushed their power into central Arabia.

In the late 300s the rulers gave up the old gods and adopted a form of Judaism. In the 520s the Jewish king Dhu Nuwas persecuted the Christians of Najran. In answer, the Christian kingdom of Aksum, egged on by Byzantium, invaded Yemen in 525 and ended the kingdom. An Aksumite general, Abraha, then ruled Yemen. Around 570 the Sasanians took it. The great Marib dam broke for the last time in the same years.
